newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees $7 billion current account surplus '96.
newsitem.headline: China sees $7 billion current account surplus '96.

text.p: China expects to post a current account surplus of about $7 billion this year, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
It also said a surplus of $19-27 billion was expected on the capital account.
The official news agency made the estimates quoting what it described as an expert at an authoritative government department.
It gave no precise comparative figures for 1995. The State Statistical Bureau has said previously that China had a balance of payments surplus last year.
Xinhua said that the capital account surplus this year would be a considerable drop from 1995 but it gave no further details.
The agency added that the twin surpluses would result in a rise in the country's foreign exchange reserves.
China previously said it had foreign exchange reserves of $90.8 billion as of July and it has estimated the total could climb to about $100 billion by the end of the year.

Earlier on Monday, an official newspaper, the China Securities Daily, said that a rise in investments under the capital account was the main contributor to the nation's rapidly expanding foreign exchange reserves.
Xinhua also said that the balance of payments surplus would have an effect on domestic interest rate levels and the value of the currency, the renminbi. It made no more precise predictions.
China has cut domestic interest rate levels twice in less than four months. The renminbi currently stands at about 8.3 to one U.S. dollar.
